blocking.title: Re-raised with new evidence: G14 can still pass while the review-run cap is exceeded, because an unlogged review can borrow the ledger entry of an earlier run that banked no review
blocking.evidence: The fix matches each banked review to some claude_review_run entry logged between 00:00 of the previous UTC day and its reviewed_at, and accepts any full matching. It never asks whether an entry already belongs to a different run. Counterexample, run against the real ship_check.g14 and make budget in a scratch repository built like the G14 test fixture (cap_share 0.2, so one review run a day, no waiver). On 2026-11-20, make review-start logs a run and the entry is committed, then the reviewer dies before banking anything (a container reclaim as in D20 is one way). On 2026-11-21, review-start logs run 1 at 00:05 and its BLOCK review is banked at 00:30. After a fix, a second review runs without review-start, which would refuse because the cap is used up (the 2026-11-11 path of D25). It is banked at 02:00 and moves the first review to history/. That is two review runs on 2026-11-21 against a cap of 1. Yet g14 returned PASS ('cash_usd = 0, caps respected') and make budget printed 'caps: all respected': the 2026-11-20 entry covers the first review and the 2026-11-21 entry covers the unlogged one. The same history without the 2026-11-20 entry fails, and so does the previous review's counterexample, so the reported path is closed but this one is not. This falsifies budget.py:656-657 ('a review skipped by make review-start cannot pass unnoticed') and README.md:209-210 ('any other overrun, whether logged or a banked review without its own logged run, fails make budget and G14'). There is a weaker second path. A review banked only in history/ (committed together with its successor) and later deleted from history/ also passes, because G14 reads every committed version of latest.json but history/ only at HEAD (ship_check.py:1601). The repository can support a sound check. D27 says each run's entry is logged when the run starts, in the commit the review covers. So match each review to an entry first added after the previous banked review's reviewed_commit and present at its own reviewed_commit, with a recorded exception for the two 2026-11-11 reviews that D25 logged after the fact. Alternatively, have review-start write a run id that the review must cite. Either way, read every committed version of every file under artifacts/review/. The current history passes such a check once this review is banked.

blocking.evidence: The first highlight says the reviewer-calibrated rule caught '0.002 [0.000, 0.013] of those that arose while small agents did ordinary tasks'. That claim is the primary-set estimate (artifacts/e2/results.json estimates, set=primary, prevalence 1e-3, 20 per 10,000: 0.00206 [0.00003, 0.01314], n_pos 1045), and 618 of those 1,045 violations are inserted. The project defines the two kinds itself (docs/REPORT.md:618-622). Natural violations 'come from small models doing ordinary tasks'. An inserted violation is 'one call chosen by the harness', and inserted ones are 'labeled synthetic ... which is why the two are reported separately'. For the violations the sentence describes, the artifact has its own row: breakdowns, by=violation_source, value=natural, n_pos 427, same estimator and same benign runs (tools/analyze.py:464-507). That row gives 0.002 [0.000, 0.020]. So the printed upper bound of 0.013 understates the described population's bound by about a third, and the highlight carries no synthetic label. Brief section 5 requires natural, inserted, and dataset violations to be reported separately, and section 9 rule 4 requires synthetic data to be labeled everywhere. The first review blocked on the same kind of pooling in a headline claim (B1). The point estimate and the qualitative contrast with Armour's records survive; the label and the interval do not. Fix it one of two ways: cite the natural-only row for this wording, or name the set as the primary set and give its synthetic share. The older sentence 'The corpus's violations arise while small agents do ordinary tasks' (README.md:141, docs/REPORT.md:506) is where the wording comes from and needs the same fix.
